_about: Nov 25 (Luka): one glossary for the whole site. Hover a term on a computer or tap it on a phone for a plain explanation (t) and, where it applies, why our number can differ from other sites (w). a = other spellings of the same label. The technical detail stays in each card's Stats explained.

ORTG.w: We count possessions from the play-by-play, so it can differ a few tenths from NBA.com.

DRTG.t: Points allowed per 100 possessions. Lower is better.
DRTG.w: We count possessions from the play-by-play, so it can differ a few tenths from NBA.com.

NET RTG.t: Points scored minus points allowed per 100 possessions. Above zero means outscoring opponents.
NET RTG.w: We count possessions from the play-by-play, so it can differ a few tenths from NBA.com.

Net, last 2 wks.t: Net rating over the last two weeks of games: who's playing well right now.

Pace.t: Possessions per 48 minutes: how fast a team plays.
Pace.w: Counted from the play-by-play, so it can differ slightly from NBA.com.

Poss.t: Times a team had the ball. Here also how much the number can be trusted: Noise under 100, Thin 100–300, Fair 300–750, Solid 750+.

Noise.t: Under 100 possessions: too few for the number to mean much yet.

Thin.t: 100–300 possessions: a hint, still easily swung by luck.

Solid.t: 750+ possessions: a number you can lean on.

Adj. net.t: Net rating with the luck of opponents' threes and free throws taken out: they count at the opponents' average instead of what they actually made.
Adj. net.w: Not an NBA.com stat; it's the Nylon Calculus luck adjustment.

RAPM.t: How many points per 100 possessions a player adds over an average player, with every teammate and opponent on the floor accounted for.
RAPM.w: Our own fit of every NBA possession with the published method (Sill, 2010). Other sites' RAPM uses different settings and seasons, so numbers differ a bit.

+/-.t: The score difference while he (or the group) was on the floor.

ON +/-.t: The team's score difference with him on the floor.

OFF +/-.t: The team's score difference with him on the bench.

ON − OFF.t: How much better (or worse) the team did with him on than off. Raw: it doesn't adjust for who he played with.

TS%.t: Scoring efficiency that counts threes and free throws: points per shooting chance.

eFG%.t: Field goal % with a made three worth 1.5 makes, since it's worth more points.

rTS%.t: True shooting compared with the NBA average. Plus is better than average.

USG%.t: Share of the team's plays he finished with a shot, free throws or a turnover while on the floor.

AST%.t: Share of teammates' made shots he assisted while on the floor.

TOV%.t: Turnovers per 100 plays used. Lower is better.

ORB%.t: Share of their own missed shots a team (or player) rebounded.

DRB%.t: Share of opponents' misses a team (or player) rebounded.

TRB%.t: Share of all missed shots rebounded while on the floor.

STL%.t: Steals per 100 opponent possessions while on the floor.

BLK%.t: Share of opponents' two-point tries blocked while on the floor.

FTA rate.t: Free throw attempts per field goal attempt: how often they get to the line.

3PAr.t: Share of field goal attempts that are threes.

Pts/poss.t: Points scored each time they had the ball.

Second chance.t: Points scored after an offensive rebound.
Second chance.w: From the NBA's official box score, so it matches NBA.com.

Fast-break points.t: Points the official scorer counts as fast-break baskets.
Fast-break points.w: A scorer's judgment call, so it won't match our transition count exactly.

Bench points.t: Points scored by players who didn't start.

PAINT.t: Points from shots inside the painted area.

Transition.t: Possessions that start with a steal or defensive rebound and end in a shot, foul or turnover within 7 seconds.
Transition.w: Our count from the play-by-play; the NBA's fast-break points is the scorer's call, so they differ.

Halfcourt.t: Every possession that isn't transition: the offense gets set up.

Clutch.t: The last five minutes with the score within five points, the NBA's definition.

Garbage time.t: Late minutes with the game decided, when starters mostly sit.
Garbage time.w: We use the Cleaning the Glass rule; other sites define it differently or not at all.

At the rim.t: Shots within 4 feet of the basket.

Long midrange.t: Two-pointers from 14 feet out to the three-point line.

Corner 3.t: Threes from along the baseline, the shortest three (22 feet).

Above-the-break 3.t: Every three that isn't from the corner (23 feet 9 inches).

0-2 ft.t: Very tight: the closest defender was within 2 feet when the shot went up.

2-4 ft.t: Tight: the closest defender was 2 to 4 feet away.

4-6 ft.t: Open: the closest defender was 4 to 6 feet away.

6+ ft.t: Wide open: no defender within 6 feet.

Unassisted FG points.t: Points from baskets he made without an assist: shots he created himself.

Putback points a game.t: Points from scoring right after an offensive rebound.

PTS CREATED.t: His own points plus the points from baskets he assisted.

Run differential.t: Unanswered scoring runs of 10 or more points: how many each team had and how much they swung games.

First 3 min.t: Score difference in the first three minutes of each quarter.

Last 3 min.t: Score difference in the last three minutes of each quarter.

Led after.t: Games the Cavs led at the end of that quarter, and their record in them.

Trailed after.t: Games the Cavs trailed at the end of that quarter, and their record in them.

Lead changes.t: Times the lead switched from one team to the other.

Times tied.t: Times the score was tied after the opening tip.

Longest lead held.t: The longest stretch one team stayed ahead without the lead changing.

Biggest run.t: The most points in a row by one team without the other scoring.

Runs and droughts.t: Runs: 8–0 or better. Droughts: 3+ minutes without a made basket.

Win chance.t: ESPN's live win probability: how often a team in that spot goes on to win.

Ball security.t: One of the four factors: turnover rate. Lower is better.

Shot quality vs shot making.t: Quality: how good the shots were, from where and how open. Making: how much better or worse they shot than that would predict.

Remaining SOS.t: How tough the rest of the schedule is: opponents' average win %. 1st = hardest.

On pace for.t: The final record if they keep winning at the same rate.

GB.t: How many games behind the team at the top of the standings.

3 games in 4 nights.t: Three games in four nights, one of the toughest stretches.

Rest edge.t: Games where the Cavs had more rest days than their opponent.

Opp rested.t: The opponent had more rest than the Cavs.

Both B2B.t: Both teams playing the second night of a back-to-back.

Opp +1 day.t: The opponent had one more day of rest.

Opp 3 in 4.t: The opponent was playing its third game in four nights.

Time-zone changes.t: Games after traveling across time zones.

Longest road trip.t: The most road games in a row.

Longest homestand.t: The most home games in a row.

Salary cap.t: The payroll line a team must be under to sign free agents with cap space.

Tax.t: Payroll over this line at season's end pays a tax that grows the further over a team is.

First apron.t: A payroll line above the tax. Teams over it lose some trade and signing tools.

Second apron.t: The highest payroll line. Teams over it lose the most trade and signing tools.

Hard cap.t: Using certain tools locks payroll under an apron for the rest of the season, no exceptions.
a: Hard capped at the first apron

Room under 1st apron.t: How much more payroll the team can add before hitting the first apron.

Projected tax bill.t: What the team would owe in luxury tax if payroll stayed where it is.
Projected tax bill.w: Tax is set on the season's final payroll, so this moves with every signing, trade and waiver.

Dead money.t: Salary still owed to players no longer on the team. It still counts on the cap.

Cap holds.t: Placeholders on the cap for the team's own free agents and unsigned picks, until they sign or are renounced.

Bird rights.t: Lets a team re-sign its own free agent even when over the cap.

Full Bird.t: Three or more seasons with the team: can be re-signed for up to the max, over the cap.

Early Bird.t: Two seasons with the team: can be re-signed over the cap, with a smaller raise limit than Full Bird.

Non-Bird.t: One season with the team: can be re-signed over the cap, but only for a modest raise.

UFA.t: Free to sign with any team.

RFA.t: Can sign an offer from another team, but his team can match it and keep him.

Two-way.t: Splits time between the Cavs and the Charge. Can be active for up to 50 NBA games and doesn't count against the cap.

games used.t: NBA games a two-way player has been active for, out of 50 a season.

Exhibit 10.t: A non-guaranteed deal that can be turned into a two-way. If he's cut and joins the Charge, he can earn a bonus.

Minimum contract.t: The lowest salary a player can sign for, set by years in the league.

Non-taxpayer mid-level.t: Lets a team over the cap sign free agents up to a set amount. Using it hard caps the team at the first apron.

Taxpayer mid-level exception.t: A smaller mid-level for teams over the first apron. Using it hard caps the team at the second apron.

Room mid-level exception.t: For teams under the cap: a signing tool left after using their cap space.

Bi-annual exception.t: A small signing tool usable every other year. Using it hard caps the team at the first apron.

Trade exception.t: A credit from sending out more salary than taken back in a trade. Lets the team absorb a player later without matching salary, until it expires.

Cash sent.t: Cash the Cavs have sent in trades this season, out of the league's yearly limit.

Draft rights.t: The Cavs control his NBA rights. He can keep playing elsewhere until they sign him.

Firsts held.t: First-round picks the Cavs own in future drafts.

Affiliate.t: A G League player on the Charge's own roster, not under an NBA contract.

Assignment.t: A Cavs player sent down to play Charge games, still on the Cavs roster.

Games missed.t: Games players sat out for an injury or illness this season, added up across the roster.
Games missed.w: Read from the NBA's official injury report before each tip; two-way players and rest days don't count.

Salary of games missed.t: Salary paid for those missed games: each player's salary divided by 82, times games missed.

Typical return.t: How long NBA players usually miss with this injury.
Typical return.w: From Hashtag Basketball's NBA injury log since 2011. A general estimate, not team guidance.

Playoff trips.t: Seasons the Cavs made the playoffs (play-in losses don't count).

FG% allowed.t: What the players he guarded shot against him.
FG% allowed.w: From NBA.com matchup tracking, which credits partial possessions.

vs their usual FG%.t: How much better or worse players shot against him than they normally do.

partial possessions guarded.t: NBA tracking splits each possession by how long he guarded each player, so these add up in fractions.

Him on.t: How the team did with him on the floor.

Him off.t: How the team did with him on the bench.

Second chances.t: What happens after an offensive rebound: the extra chances (and points) from grabbing their own misses.

FG%.t: Share of shots made, threes and twos together.
